items.title: David Finck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 29, 2015
items.q: The interviewee expresses high admiration for Marcus Miller's playing ('fantastic electric bass player', 'one of my all-time favorites') and mentions seeing him perform on a jazz cruise, but does not state they have met, collaborated, or played together.

ctx.x: Yeah. And it’s funny from a bass player standpoint too, that that part of music has become so predominant. You know, when a car goes by you and you hear the [scats] I sometimes wonder well what does a bass player think of that. Are they happy about that?

That bass line functions in that piece most of the time. I mean usually there’s a drum loop and there’s a bass line that works, and I don’t really like it because most of them aren’t really inventive or creative in any way. And most of the time it’s not even a bass player. The bass player Marcus Miller is a fantastic electric bass player. And actually he plays acoustic bass also, which is a little frightening for me, because he’s something else. He has played classic bass lines on songs where I go that is…
Well that reminds me of when my father would come into the room when I was playing The Beatles and he’d go, “what’s wrong with your record player?” Some things never change.
